dynamicPorts.description: This is the Function node. Input and output ports are discovered from the user script in the "functionScript" parameter, and the connectable port NAME carries a prefix the script does not: reading "Inputs.xyz" creates the input port "in-xyz", assigning "Outputs.xyz" creates the output port "out-xyz", and calling "Outputs.xyz()" creates the signal output "out-xyz". The property panel and the port list show the unprefixed display name ("xyz"), so connect to "in-xyz"/"out-xyz" — a connection written to the bare script name silently targets a port that does not exist. The node's own static ports ("run", "done", "success", "failure", "completed", "unchanged", "error") are never prefixed, so "Outputs.done()" is the separate port "out-done". The Script node ("Javascript2") does NOT prefix; that convention belongs to this node alone.

inputs.name: delimiter
inputs.description: The character between cells. Use ; for a European export, or a tab for TSV

inputs.name: hasHeader
inputs.description: When ticked the first row names the columns and Items is an array of records. Untick it and Items is an array of rows, each an array of cells

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The CSV text to parse. A leading byte-order mark — which is what Excel writes when it saves UTF-8 — is stripped, so the first column keeps its name

outputs.name: changed
outputs.description: Fires once Items and Count hold the freshly parsed CSV

outputs.name: count
outputs.description: How many rows the last successful parse produced, not counting the header row

outputs.name: error
outputs.description: Why the CSV could not be parsed, naming the line it gave up on; empty until a parse fails

outputs.name: failure
outputs.description: Fires when the CSV could not be parsed, leaving Items and Count as they were

outputs.name: items
outputs.description: The parsed rows — records when Has Header is ticked, arrays of cells when it is not. Every cell is a string, including columns that look numeric. Unchanged while the CSV cannot be parsed

inputs.name: extract
inputs.description: Runs Pattern over Text and reports what it found

inputs.name: extractAll
inputs.description: Collects every match into Matches instead of stopping at the first one

inputs.name: flags
inputs.description: Regex flags i, m, s, u and y; g is controlled by Extract All and a g written here is ignored

inputs.name: pattern
inputs.description: A JavaScript regular expression without the surrounding slashes; capture groups appear on Groups

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The text to search

outputs.name: completed
outputs.description: Fires after every invocation, whatever the outcome — wire this to carry on regardless. Failure still fires and still carries its reason, so this cannot hide an error

outputs.name: done
outputs.description: Fires once the extract has run, whether it matched or not — Found and Not Found say which

outputs.name: error
outputs.description: Why the pattern could not be used: it is blank, or it is not a valid regular expression

outputs.name: failure
outputs.description: Fires when the pattern itself is unusable, which is a bug to fix rather than a result

outputs.name: firstGroup
outputs.description: The first capture group of the first match, which is the whole answer for a pattern like (\d+)%

outputs.name: found
outputs.description: Fires when the pattern ran and matched at least once

outputs.name: groups
outputs.description: Capture groups of the first match; an optional group that did not participate is a blank string, not a hole

outputs.name: match
outputs.description: The first match, or blank when nothing matched

outputs.name: matchCount
outputs.description: How many matches were found, which is at most one unless Extract All is on

outputs.name: matches
outputs.description: Every match when Extract All is on, otherwise just the first

outputs.name: namedGroups
outputs.description: Named capture groups of the first match, keyed by name

outputs.name: notFound
outputs.description: Fires when the pattern ran and matched nothing, which is an ordinary outcome rather than a mistake

inputs.name: encoding
inputs.description: How the bytes are rendered as text. Base64 URL is the safe one for a URL or a token

inputs.name: generate
inputs.description: Generates a fresh block of random bytes

inputs.name: length
inputs.description: How many random BYTES to generate (not characters — hex renders each byte as two). 1 to 4096

outputs.name: completed
outputs.description: Fires after every invocation, whatever the outcome — wire this to carry on regardless. Failure still fires and still carries its reason, so this cannot hide an error

outputs.name: done
outputs.description: Fires once fresh random bytes are available on Value

outputs.name: error
outputs.description: Why no random bytes were produced

outputs.name: failure
outputs.description: Fires when there is no cryptographic random source here, or Length is out of range. This node will not quietly substitute Math.random()

outputs.name: value
outputs.description: The random bytes rendered in Encoding, replaced on every New

ssr.note: An event stream cannot be consumed during a server render; the node connects in the browser after hydration.

inputs.name: autoConnect
inputs.description: Opens the stream as soon as a URL is available, without waiting for a Connect signal

inputs.name: autoReconnect
inputs.description: Retries after a failure with a growing backoff; turning it off reports the failure and stops

inputs.name: body
inputs.description: Request body, sent as JSON unless it is already a string; ignored for GET and HEAD

inputs.name: connect
inputs.description: Opens the stream, replacing any connection already open and resetting the retry count

inputs.name: dedupeById
inputs.description: Drops events whose id has already been seen, so a reconnect that resumes cannot re-deliver messages

inputs.name: disconnect
inputs.description: Closes the stream and stops retrying

inputs.name: eventTypes
inputs.description: Comma-separated named event types to subscribe to; only needed for the EventSource transport, as Fetch delivers every type

inputs.name: headers
inputs.description: Request headers as an object, for bearer tokens and the like; ignored by the EventSource transport, which cannot set them

inputs.name: maxReconnectDelay
inputs.description: Ceiling on the backoff in milliseconds, however many failures there have been

inputs.name: maxRetries
inputs.description: Consecutive failures allowed before the connection gives up and reports an error; 0 keeps retrying

inputs.name: method
inputs.description: HTTP method for the request; anything other than GET needs the Fetch transport

inputs.name: reconnectDelay
inputs.description: First retry delay in milliseconds, doubling per consecutive failure up to Max Reconnect Delay

inputs.name: reconnectOnStreamEnd
inputs.description: Reconnects when the server closes the stream cleanly; off by default because reconnecting an agent stream re-issues the request

inputs.name: textPath
inputs.description: Where the text lives inside a JSON payload, as a dot path such as choices.0.delta.content; leave blank for a stream of bare text

inputs.name: transport
inputs.description: How the stream is fetched: Fetch carries headers and a body, EventSource lets the browser handle reconnection, Auto prefers Fetch

inputs.name: url
inputs.description: Endpoint to stream from; changing it while connected reconnects to the new one

inputs.name: withCredentials
inputs.description: Sends cookies and HTTP auth to a cross-origin endpoint, which the server must also allow

outputs.name: completed
outputs.description: Fires after every invocation, whatever the outcome — wire this to carry on regardless. Failure still fires and still carries its reason, so this cannot hide an error

outputs.name: connected
outputs.description: True only while the stream is open and frames may arrive

outputs.name: connectionState
outputs.description: Where the connection is: idle, connecting, open, reconnecting, closed or error

outputs.name: data
outputs.description: The event payload, parsed as JSON when it is JSON and handed over as text when it is not

outputs.name: deliverySemantics
outputs.description: What this stream actually guarantees, derived from whether the server sends ids: at-most-once, at-least-once or at-least-once-deduped

outputs.name: done
outputs.description: Fires when the action finished: a Connect whose stream opened, or a Disconnect that stopped one

outputs.name: duplicatesSuppressed
outputs.description: How many replayed events Dedupe By Id has dropped on this connection

outputs.name: eventType
outputs.description: The event name the server sent, or message when it sent none

outputs.name: failure
outputs.description: Fires when the stream could not be opened, or gave up retrying. Last Error carries the reason

outputs.name: lastError
outputs.description: What went wrong most recently, including the reason a retry was scheduled

outputs.name: lastEventId
outputs.description: The furthest id the server has reported, which is the point a reconnect resumes from

outputs.name: lastMessageTime
outputs.description: When the last event arrived, as milliseconds since the epoch; useful for spotting a stalled stream

outputs.name: messageCount
outputs.description: How many events have been delivered on this connection, not counting suppressed duplicates

outputs.name: onClose
outputs.description: Fires when the stream has stopped for good, whether it ended cleanly or gave up

outputs.name: onError
outputs.description: Fires when the stream failed or dropped, whether or not a retry is going to follow

outputs.name: onMessage
outputs.description: Fires once per event, after Data, Raw and Text already hold it

outputs.name: onOpen
outputs.description: Fires when the stream has been established

outputs.name: raw
outputs.description: The event payload exactly as it arrived, before any parsing

outputs.name: retryCount
outputs.description: Consecutive failed attempts in the current outage; back to zero once the stream opens

outputs.name: text
outputs.description: The one data output guaranteed to be a string: Raw when no Text Path is set, the field at that path when one is, blank when it does not resolve

outputs.name: unchanged
outputs.description: Fires when there was nothing to do: a Disconnect with no stream running, or a Connect a later Connect or Disconnect superseded before it opened

inputs.name: properties
inputs.description: Names of the values this node writes, each becoming an input to supply it

inputs.name: store
inputs.description: Writes every supplied property value into the component object

outputs.name: completed
outputs.description: Fires after every invocation. This node has no other outcome — no Unchanged and no Failure — so it always fires together with Done, and wiring either one does the same thing. It is here on every action so that reaching for it is never a per-node decision

outputs.name: done
outputs.description: Fires once every property has been written

dynamicPorts.description: Property input ports follow the "properties" parameter.

outputs.name: completed

variables.property: one of the comma-separated entries in the `properties` parameter
one of the comma-separated entries in the `properties` parameter

inputs.name: clearHistory
inputs.description: Throws the history away and starts again from the live state

inputs.name: coalesceMs
inputs.description: Window in milliseconds within which successive changes to the same keys fold into one undo step; 0 records every change separately

inputs.name: enabled
inputs.description: Turning this off pauses recording and keeps the entries already collected

inputs.name: maxHistory
inputs.description: How many entries to keep before the oldest is dropped, never below two and never dropping the current one

inputs.name: storeName
inputs.description: Names the global store to record; one tracker per store is enough, and two on the same store share one history

inputs.name: trackKeys
inputs.description: Comma-separated keys to record; leave blank to record the whole store, and note that changing this clears the history

outputs.name: byReferenceKeys
outputs.description: Comma-separated keys an undo cannot fully restore because they hold live objects rather than data

outputs.name: canRedo
outputs.description: True when an undo has been made and there is a later entry to step forward to

outputs.name: canUndo
outputs.description: True when there is an earlier entry to step back to

outputs.name: completed
outputs.description: Fires after every invocation, whatever the outcome — wire this to carry on regardless. Failure still fires and still carries its reason, so this cannot hide an error

outputs.name: currentIndex
outputs.description: Where in the history the store is sitting; -1 when nothing is being tracked

outputs.name: done
outputs.description: Fires once the history has been thrown away and re-baselined from the live state

outputs.name: fullyRestorable
outputs.description: False when some entry holds a Collection, a Model or a function, which a snapshot can only keep by reference

outputs.name: history
outputs.description: One entry per recorded change, each with its index, timestamp, description and changed keys, but not its state

outputs.name: historyChanged
outputs.description: Fires whenever an entry is added, the position moves, or the history is cleared

outputs.name: historySize
outputs.description: How many entries the history holds, including the baseline it started from

outputs.name: unchanged
outputs.description: Fires when there was nothing to throw away, because the history was already just its baseline

inputs.name: jumpTo
inputs.description: Moves the store to the entry named by Target Index

inputs.name: redo
inputs.description: Steps the store forward one entry, or fires Unchanged when it is already at the end

inputs.name: storeName
inputs.description: Names the store to step through; a State History node must already be tracking it

inputs.name: targetIndex
inputs.description: Entry to move to when Jump To is signalled, counting from zero; ignored by Undo and Redo

inputs.name: undo
inputs.description: Steps the store back one entry, or fires Unchanged when it is already at the beginning

outputs.name: byReferenceKeys
outputs.description: Comma-separated keys the restored entry put back as the same live object rather than as a copy

outputs.name: completed
outputs.description: Fires after every invocation, whatever the outcome — wire this to carry on regardless. Failure still fires and still carries its reason, so this cannot hide an error

outputs.name: done
outputs.description: Fires when the step actually moved the store

outputs.name: error
outputs.description: Why the last step failed; blank once one succeeds

outputs.name: failure
outputs.description: Fires when the step could not be made, because nothing is tracking the store or Target Index is outside the history

outputs.name: fullyRestorable
outputs.description: False when the entry just restored held live objects a snapshot could only keep by reference

outputs.name: jumped
outputs.description: Fires once the store holds the entry Target Index named

outputs.name: redone
outputs.description: Fires when a step forward actually happened, and not when the history was already at its end

outputs.name: unchanged
outputs.description: Fires when the history had nowhere to go — an Undo at the beginning or a Redo at the end. Not a failure: this is an ordinary end-stop, and it used to be silent

outputs.name: undone
outputs.description: Fires when a step back actually happened, and not when the history was already at its beginning

inputs.name: restore
inputs.description: Puts a checkpoint back as an ordinary write, so it appears in the history and can itself be undone

inputs.name: save
inputs.description: Copies the store as it is now and keeps it under Snapshot Name

inputs.name: snapshotData
inputs.description: A previously exported Snapshot to restore instead of the named one; leave blank to restore by name

inputs.name: snapshotName
inputs.description: Name to save this checkpoint under, and the name Restore looks up; required to save

inputs.name: storeName
inputs.description: Names the store to snapshot or restore into

outputs.name: byReferenceKeys
outputs.description: Comma-separated keys the checkpoint holds as live objects, so restoring will not undo changes made to them since

outputs.name: completed
outputs.description: Fires after every invocation, whatever the outcome — wire this to carry on regardless. Failure still fires and still carries its reason, so this cannot hide an error

outputs.name: done
outputs.description: Fires once a Save or Restore you triggered has finished, whichever of the two it was

outputs.name: error
outputs.description: Why the last save or restore failed; blank once one succeeds

outputs.name: failure
outputs.description: Fires when the checkpoint could not be saved or put back, most often an unnamed or unknown checkpoint

outputs.name: fullyRestorable
outputs.description: False when the checkpoint holds a Collection, a Model or a function, which it can only keep by reference

outputs.name: restored
outputs.description: Fires once the store holds the checkpoint again

outputs.name: saved
outputs.description: Fires once the checkpoint has been taken and Snapshot holds it

outputs.name: snapshot
outputs.description: The checkpoint just saved or restored, as plain data that can be written to a file and fed back into Snapshot Data

ssr.note: Interval-based flushing needs a running timer, so it only happens in the browser. Add, Flush and size-based flushing behave normally.

inputs.name: add
inputs.description: Buffers the current Data, flushing straight away if that reaches Flush Size

inputs.name: clear
inputs.description: Discards the buffer and resets both counters without flushing

inputs.name: data
inputs.description: The next item to buffer, of any type; its value is retained between pulses of Add

inputs.name: flush
inputs.description: Hands the whole buffer to Flushed Data now; an empty buffer is a legitimate no-op

inputs.name: flushInterval
inputs.description: Flush automatically this often in milliseconds while items are buffered; 0 disables interval flushing

inputs.name: flushSize
inputs.description: Flush automatically once this many items are buffered; 0 disables size-based flushing

inputs.name: maxSize
inputs.description: Hard cap on buffered items; overflow drops the oldest and is counted on Dropped Items; 0 means no cap

outputs.name: buffer
outputs.description: Items waiting to be flushed, oldest first

outputs.name: bufferSize
outputs.description: How many items are waiting, which is what Flush Size is compared against

outputs.name: cleared
outputs.description: Fires once the buffer has been discarded

outputs.name: completed
outputs.description: Fires after every invocation, whatever the outcome — wire this to carry on regardless. Failure still fires and still carries its reason, so this cannot hide an error

outputs.name: done
outputs.description: Fires once an Add, Flush or Clear you triggered has changed the buffer

outputs.name: droppedItems
outputs.description: How many items Max Size has discarded from the front since the last Clear

outputs.name: error
outputs.description: Why the last Add was refused; blank until one is

outputs.name: failure
outputs.description: Fires when Add ran before any value had arrived on Data, so nothing was buffered

outputs.name: flushCount
outputs.description: How many flushes have happened since the last Clear

outputs.name: flushed
outputs.description: Fires once Flushed Data holds a new batch, and not for a flush that found nothing

outputs.name: flushedData
outputs.description: The batch handed over by the most recent flush; a stable array that later Adds do not mutate

outputs.name: overflowed
outputs.description: Fires when Max Size has just discarded something

outputs.name: unchanged
outputs.description: Fires when a Flush found nothing to send, or a Clear found nothing to discard — an idle buffer doing exactly what it should

inputs.name: add
inputs.description: Appends the current Chunk, which is retained between pulses, so a second Add with no new chunk appends it again

inputs.name: chunk
inputs.description: The next fragment of text to append; wire a stream Text output, not its Data output, which is JSON-parsed and is usually an object

inputs.name: clear
inputs.description: Empties the buffer, the messages and both dropped counts

inputs.name: delimiter
inputs.description: Message boundary to split complete messages off; leave empty to accumulate everything, which is what a token stream wants

inputs.name: maxLength
inputs.description: Cap on the pending buffer in characters; overflow drops the oldest and is counted on Dropped Characters

inputs.name: maxMessages
inputs.description: Cap on retained complete messages, oldest dropped first; 0 keeps them all, which grows forever

outputs.name: accumulated
outputs.description: Everything appended since the last Clear that has not yet been split off as a complete message

outputs.name: byteCount
outputs.description: Length of Accumulated in UTF-8 bytes, which differs from Character Count for anything outside ASCII

outputs.name: changed
outputs.description: Fires whenever an Add appended something, which is the cue to redraw

outputs.name: characterCount
outputs.description: Length of Accumulated in characters

outputs.name: cleared
outputs.description: Fires once the buffer and the messages have been emptied

outputs.name: completed
outputs.description: Fires after every invocation, whatever the outcome — wire this to carry on regardless. Failure still fires and still carries its reason, so this cannot hide an error

outputs.name: done
outputs.description: Fires once an Add or Clear you triggered has changed the buffer

outputs.name: droppedCharacters
outputs.description: How many characters Max Length has discarded from the front since the last Clear

outputs.name: droppedMessages
outputs.description: How many complete messages Max Messages has discarded since the last Clear

outputs.name: error
outputs.description: Why the last chunk was refused; blank once a chunk of text arrives

outputs.name: failure
outputs.description: Fires when a chunk was not text and nothing was appended, which usually means the wrong stream output is wired

outputs.name: lastMessage
outputs.description: The most recent complete message, which is what a chat surface usually wants

outputs.name: messageCount
outputs.description: How many complete messages are being retained, which is not how many have arrived

outputs.name: messageReceived
outputs.description: Fires once per Add that completed at least one message, not once per message

outputs.name: messages
outputs.description: Complete messages split off the delimiter, oldest first, capped at Max Messages

outputs.name: overflowed
outputs.description: Fires when Max Length or Max Messages has just discarded something

outputs.name: unchanged
outputs.description: Fires when an Add had no text to append — an empty chunk, or one already refused — or a Clear found nothing to discard

inputs.name: columns
inputs.description: Which properties to write, in order, comma separated. Leave it empty and every property found on the records is written, in the order they were first seen

inputs.name: delimiter
inputs.description: The character between cells. Any cell containing it is quoted automatically

inputs.name: includeHeader
inputs.description: Write the column names as the first row

inputs.name: items
inputs.description: The array to write. Records become rows; an array of arrays is written cell for cell

outputs.name: changed
outputs.description: Fires once CSV holds the freshly written text

outputs.name: count
outputs.description: How many data rows were written, not counting the header row

outputs.name: text
outputs.description: The array as CSV text. Cells containing the delimiter, a quote or a newline are quoted and their quotes doubled, so this round-trips back through Parse CSV unchanged

inputs.name: generate
inputs.description: Generates a fresh UUID, replacing the one on Id

outputs.name: completed
outputs.description: Fires after every invocation, whatever the outcome — wire this to carry on regardless. Failure still fires and still carries its reason, so this cannot hide an error

outputs.name: done
outputs.description: Fires once a new UUID is available on Id

outputs.name: error
outputs.description: Why no UUID could be generated

outputs.name: failure
outputs.description: Fires when there is no cryptographic random source here, leaving Id as it was

outputs.name: uuid
outputs.description: A random version-4 UUID, generated once when the node is created and again on every New. Use this rather than Unique Id wherever the id has to be globally unique or unguessable

ssr.note: A WebSocket cannot be meaningfully opened during a server render and would leak a socket per request; the node connects in the browser after hydration.

inputs.name: autoConnect
inputs.description: Connect as soon as a URL is available, without waiting for a Connect signal

inputs.name: autoReconnect
inputs.description: Retries after an unsolicited close with a growing backoff; turning it off reports the close as an error

inputs.name: connect
inputs.description: Opens the socket, replacing one already open without reporting a close

inputs.name: disconnect
inputs.description: Closes the socket and cancels any pending reconnect

inputs.name: heartbeatInterval
inputs.description: Milliseconds between heartbeats while the socket is open; 0 disables it, and only enable it if your server expects the message

inputs.name: heartbeatMessage
inputs.description: Application text sent as the heartbeat; it is not a protocol ping frame

inputs.name: heartbeatReply
inputs.description: Exact text the server answers a heartbeat with; it is measured as Latency, hidden from On Message, and its absence is treated as a dead connection

inputs.name: jitter
inputs.description: Spreads reconnect attempts randomly across the second half of each backoff window, so a fleet does not return in lockstep

inputs.name: maxQueueSize
inputs.description: Messages the queue holds before further Sends are refused and counted as dropped; 0 or less is unlimited and can grow during a long outage

inputs.name: maxReconnectDelay
inputs.description: Ceiling on the backoff in milliseconds, however many attempts there have been

inputs.name: maxRetries
inputs.description: Reconnect attempts allowed per outage; 0 disables retrying and a negative value means unlimited

inputs.name: message
inputs.description: Value to send; objects are JSON-serialised, and ArrayBuffers and typed arrays go as binary frames

inputs.name: messageType
inputs.description: Auto sends binary values as binary and everything else as text; Binary encodes text and objects as UTF-8 first

inputs.name: protocols
inputs.description: Comma-separated WebSocket subprotocols to offer during the handshake

inputs.name: reconnectDelay
inputs.description: First backoff delay in milliseconds; each further attempt doubles it up to Max Reconnect Delay

inputs.name: send
inputs.description: Hands the current Message to the socket, or applies the When Disconnected policy

inputs.name: url
inputs.description: Endpoint to connect to, which must start with ws:// or wss://; changing it reconnects to the new one

inputs.name: whenDisconnected
inputs.description: What a Send does while the socket is not open: hold it in order, discard and count it, or also report an error

outputs.name: closeCode
outputs.description: WebSocket close code from the last close, or 1006 when the socket died without one

outputs.name: closeReason
outputs.description: Reason the server gave for closing, which is often blank

outputs.name: completed
outputs.description: Fires after every invocation, whatever the outcome — wire this to carry on regardless. Failure still fires and still carries its reason, so this cannot hide an error

outputs.name: connected
outputs.description: True only while the socket is open and messages can be sent without queueing

outputs.name: connectionState
outputs.description: Where the connection is: idle, connecting, open, reconnecting, closed or error

outputs.name: done
outputs.description: Fires when the action finished: a Connect whose socket opened, a Send accepted for delivery (sent, or queued for the next open), or a Disconnect that closed something

outputs.name: droppedCount
outputs.description: Messages that will never be sent, whether discarded by policy, by a full queue, or by the node being removed

outputs.name: failure
outputs.description: Fires when the action could not be performed — no URL, a URL that is not ws:// or wss://, a connection that gave up, or a refused Send. Last Error carries the reason

outputs.name: lastError
outputs.description: What went wrong most recently, including why a reconnect was scheduled or abandoned

outputs.name: latency
outputs.description: Round trip of the last heartbeat in milliseconds; 0 until one has been measured

outputs.name: onClose
outputs.description: Fires whenever the socket goes down, whether or not a reconnect is going to follow

outputs.name: onError
outputs.description: Fires when something went wrong: a failed connect, a refused send, a dead heartbeat, or a give-up

outputs.name: onMessage
outputs.description: Fires once per message, after Received already holds it; heartbeat replies are not messages

outputs.name: onMessageSent
outputs.description: Fires when a message has been handed to the socket, including a queued one flushed on reopen; not for heartbeats

outputs.name: onOpen
outputs.description: Fires every time the socket opens, including after a reconnect

outputs.name: onReconnect
outputs.description: Fires on every open after the first; a WebSocket cannot resume, so this is the cue to re-fetch rather than assume continuity

outputs.name: queueSize
outputs.description: Messages held because the socket was not open when Send ran

outputs.name: received
outputs.description: The last message, parsed as JSON when it is JSON and handed over as text when it is not

outputs.name: receivedIsBinary
outputs.description: True when the last message was a binary frame, in which case Received holds the buffer

outputs.name: receivedRaw
outputs.description: The last text message exactly as it arrived; blank for a binary frame

outputs.name: retryCount
outputs.description: Attempts made during the current outage; back to zero once the socket opens

outputs.name: unchanged
outputs.description: Fires when there was nothing to do: a Disconnect with nothing open, a Send discarded by the Drop policy, or a Connect a later Connect or Disconnect superseded before it opened

ssr.note: The scheduler clock is frozen during server render; the value stays at its start and Finished never fires there.

inputs.name: delay
inputs.description: How long to wait before the move begins, in milliseconds

inputs.name: duration
inputs.description: How long the move takes, in milliseconds

inputs.name: easingCurve
inputs.description: Shape of the movement between where the value is and Target Value

inputs.name: targetValue
inputs.description: Value to move towards; the first one to arrive is adopted outright rather than animated to

outputs.name: atTargetValue
outputs.description: Fires when the value settles on Target Value, and not at all if a new target interrupted it

outputs.name: currentValue
outputs.description: Where the move has got to, updated every frame while it runs

inputs.name: alignX
inputs.description: Horizontal alignment of this element within the space its parent gives it

inputs.name: alignY
inputs.description: Vertical alignment of this element within the space its parent gives it

inputs.name: backgroundColor
inputs.description: Fill colour behind the label and icon

inputs.name: blockTouch
inputs.description: Stops every pointer event that lands on this control from reaching the nodes it sits inside. Blunt: it takes hover and pointer-down with it, so reach for Click Bubbling first if it is only clicks you want to keep in

inputs.name: borderBottomColor
inputs.description: Colour of the bottom edge only, overriding Border Color

inputs.name: borderBottomLeftRadius
inputs.description: Rounds the bottom-left corner only, overriding Corner Radius

inputs.name: borderBottomRightRadius
inputs.description: Rounds the bottom-right corner only, overriding Corner Radius

inputs.name: borderBottomStyle
inputs.description: Line style for the bottom edge only, overriding Border Style; None hides that edge

inputs.name: borderBottomWidth
inputs.description: Thickness of the bottom edge in pixels, and it adds to the element's size

inputs.name: borderColor
inputs.description: Colour of the border, which has no effect while Border Style is None

inputs.name: borderLeftColor
inputs.description: Colour of the left edge only, overriding Border Color

inputs.name: borderLeftStyle
inputs.description: Line style for the left edge only, overriding Border Style; None hides that edge

inputs.name: borderLeftWidth
inputs.description: Thickness of the left edge in pixels, and it adds to the element's size

inputs.name: borderRadius
inputs.description: Rounds all four corners, except any corner that sets its own radius

inputs.name: borderRightColor
